newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on RBI's low-key role.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on RBI's low-key role.

text.p: The Indian rupee broke through the 35.75 per dollar barrier on Thursday and closed at 35.745/755 compared to its 35.75/76 opening, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made a half-hearted bid to arrest the rupee's rise by buying dollars in the morning session when the rupee pierced the 35.75 mark.
The rupee had risen to 35.745 when RBI intervened.
The RBI did not intervene in the spot market later, allowing the rupee to trade at the 35.74 level for the rest of the day.

"There was good amount of export sale (of dollars) today," said the chief dealer at a foreign bank. "There was good inward (remittances) too, probably from FIIs (foreign institutional investors on Indian stock exchanges)," he said.
The forward premiums opened higher, reflecting a large outflow of funds from the banking system in the next few days.
"However, steady call money rate of 0.25 percent today encouraged banks to add to their received position," said a dealer, referring to banks receiving a premium against sale of forward dollar.
RBI intervened in the forward dollar market, buying June and August dollars on Thursday, dealers said.
The six-month annualised forward premium inched up to close at 4.36 percent compared to the previous close of 4.25 percent.
Exporters confirmed that the expectation of the rupee staying firm in the short-term influenced their behaviour.
"We are keeping imports uncovered," said R.K. Das, chief of treasury and forex at Adani Exports, a leading export firm.
"Looks like the rupee will keep appreciating," he said.
